data.narrative:
Teradar is a Series B defense & security company founded by MIT-trained leadership (CEO Matt Carey) with deep domain expertise in terahertz sensing and chip architecture. The valuation assessment draws on a comparable universe of 8 private peers and 2 public companies operating in the same sector and stage.

Two methods inform the triangulation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $175M in total capital raised, implying a $332M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines 8 same-sector, same-stage private companies—Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B) among them—yielding a median valuation of $1.1B and a range spanning $300M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a triangulated range of $283M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $729M. This wide dispersion reflects genuine uncertainty around Teradar's position within the peer set. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively on capital deployed; the peer-median approach captures market valuations but relies on comparability assumptions across companies with differing revenue profiles and market traction. Key uncertainties include Teradar's revenue and growth trajectory relative to named peers, and the extent to which frontier-stage terahertz IP commands a premium within the defense sector.
